Next after #19 (Jack, 2026-10-21): separate pools from on-demand. A pool is the machines you own, each with a committed cost and an expiry (the Mini: $0, never; an SF Compute window: its price, its stop). An on-demand is a machine template plus a budget (machines at once, price ceiling, maybe dollars per period). Launch names where work runs: --pool, --ondemand (or --rent), or both (owned first, then rent). Accounting reports committed / used / idle per kind. Open: flag name; per-period dollar budget. Notes: scratch/pools-and-ondemand.md in the cfdaa1 worktree.
